waves.name: Foundations and immutable context
waves.gateToAdvance: The live champion is reproducible and correctly labeled, source contracts are immutable and as-of safe, and 2020-2025 roster/team context passes coverage checks.

acceptance: One reproducible live champion model version and ranking artifact is designated for V2 comparisons.
Ingestion, redraft, Best Ball, draft-room, advisor, and explainer surfaces report the same champion identity.
The frozen artifact records scoring format, source snapshot identifiers, model version, row count, digest, and creation time.
Freezing and relabeling the champion does not change player projections or ranking order.

waves.name: Chronological validation framework
waves.gateToAdvance: Rolling-origin evaluation, preregistered metrics, paired intervals, leakage checks, deterministic seeds, and reproducible artifacts are operational before V2 fitting.

targets.name: Build the rolling-origin backtest harness
acceptance: Evaluation seasons use only earlier eligible training seasons and a declared preseason cutoff.
The harness scores team-week, player-week, season-total, and roster-simulation artifacts without reading future data.
Runs persist configuration, model version, seed, source snapshot identifiers, cohort counts, and output digest.
A stored run replays to identical results.

evidence.result: Implemented an expanding-window rolling-origin harness with six frozen preseason cutoffs, strict prior-season training eligibility, prediction/outcome isolation, and one identity-matched scoring envelope for team-week, player-week, season-total, and roster-simulation artifacts. Definitive metrics remain explicitly deferred to V2-005.

targets.name: Implement the definitive metric suite
acceptance: Metrics include team-opportunity MAE and bias, a proper distribution score, P10/P50/P90 coverage, season-total MAE and bias, Top-12 precision and recall, spike recall, counted Best Ball points, and draft-decision regret.
Results include sample sizes and paired bootstrap confidence intervals using a declared resampling unit.
Metrics are reported overall and for required position, rookie, changed-team, injury, and small-sample cohorts.
Champion, simple baseline, market baseline where eligible, challenger, and required ablations remain separately labeled.

evidence.reference: model/ff_v2_metrics.py; model/ff_v2_backtest.py; docs/fantasy-football-v2-metric-suite.md
evidence.result: Preregistered and implemented the definitive model-agnostic metric suite before V2 fitting: eight team-opportunity pools with MAE, bias, P10/P50/P90 weighted interval score and coverage; Week 1-17 season MAE/bias and Top-12 precision/recall; position-aware spike recall; Best Ball counted points; and non-negative draft-decision regret. Frozen tolerances, material-degradation bounds, missing-cohort rules, and market eligibility are part of the executable policy.

Missing distributions or cohorts fail closed rather than receiving invented scores.

The champion-versus-challenger protocol is frozen before Team Opportunity is fitted.

waves.name: Team opportunity forecast
waves.gateToAdvance: Every team-week has calibrated and reproducible plays, attempts, carry, target, and touchdown pools with coherent uncertainty and explicit fallbacks.

targets.name: Define and persist team opportunity facts and forecasts
acceptance: Count semantics distinguish plays, pass attempts, allocatable targets, rush attempts, RB carries, RB targets, passing touchdowns, and rushing touchdowns.
Historical team-week facts and versioned forecast distributions persist source and model provenance.
Quarterback kneels, scrambles, sacks, throwaways, and non-RB carries are handled by documented reconciliation rules.
Schema and ingestion tests cover duplicate identity, missing games, and idempotent refresh.

evidence.reference: ingest/ff_v2_team_opportunity.py; db/schema.py; web/src/db/schema.ts; web/src/db/ensure-schema.ts; docs/fantasy-football-v2-team-opportunity-contract.md
evidence.result: Implemented immutable forecast-run, team-game envelope, and long-form opportunity-distribution contracts with deterministic digests, model/source/as-of provenance, required pool validation, and documented play, attempt, target, RB, touchdown, kneel, scramble, sack, throwaway, and non-RB carry semantics.

evidence.reference: python -m pytest tests/test_ff_v2_team_opportunity.py tests/test_ff_v2_historical_context.py -q; python -m compileall -q ingest/ff_v2_team_opportunity.py; cd web && npx tsc --noEmit; independent adversarial probes
evidence.result: Independent verification passed 12 focused tests, Python compilation, and TypeScript compilation. Duplicate facts/forecasts, missing games, incomplete or invalid distributions, tampering, undeclared snapshots, missing provenance, invalid fallbacks, and non-finite values fail closed; identical artifacts refresh idempotently.

evidence.reference: configured-database schema and reconciliation audit; independent V2-007 verifier
evidence.result: All three forecast tables exist. All 3,230 historical team-game facts satisfy plays = pass attempts + sacks + rush attempts and the target/RB subset constraints. Forecast tables correctly contain zero fitted rows because fitting begins only in V2-008. All four V2-007 acceptance criteria passed with no blocker.

targets.name: Forecast coherent team opportunity distributions
acceptance: The model forecasts weekly plays, attempts, allocatable targets, RB carries, RB targets, passing touchdowns, and rushing touchdowns with expected value, dispersion, P10, P50, and P90.
Game-script outcomes are jointly coherent rather than independently sampled counts.
Team, opponent, quarterback, and play-caller evidence is shrunk appropriately for sample size.
Fallback tiers A, B, and C are recorded and widen uncertainty when context is missing.

evidence.reference: model/ff_v2_team_opportunity.py; tests/test_ff_v2_team_opportunity_model.py; docs/fantasy-football-v2-team-opportunity-model.md
evidence.result: Implemented a recency-weighted, sample-size-shrunk hierarchical model for all required pools. Shared seeded game pace, scoring, and complementary script latents drive per-team plays, dropbacks/sacks/rushes, attempts/targets/RB work, and passing/rushing touchdown splits; every draw reconciles before EV, dispersion, P10, P50, and P90 are summarized.

evidence.reference: diagnostic run c6721951-dccd-5702-82c0-de8cc4d83b29; source-snapshot availability audit
evidence.result: A deterministic 544-forecast diagnostic run exposed that exact play-by-play and weekly-stat snapshots postdated the simulated preseason cutoff. It is not accepted as chronological evidence or committed as a canonical artifact; the historical CLI now fails closed on those snapshots.

evidence.reference: python -m pytest tests/test_ff_champion_baseline.py tests/test_ff_source_contracts.py tests/test_ff_v2_historical_context.py tests/test_ff_v2_backtest.py tests/test_ff_v2_metrics.py tests/test_ff_v2_historical_bestball_cohort.py tests/test_ff_v2_audits.py tests/test_ff_v2_team_opportunity.py tests/test_ff_v2_team_opportunity_model.py -q
evidence.result: Eighty combined V2 tests passed, including per-draw conservation, touchdown-to-opportunity bounds, complementary opponent scripts, normalized scenario probabilities, deterministic and order-independent replay, sample-aware shrinkage, held-out-outcome rejection, exact source-snapshot cutoff rejection, sparse Tier C behavior, and A/B/C uncertainty ordering.

evidence.reference: independent V2-008 statistical design review; canonical artifact fallback audit
evidence.result: The canonical reconstruction does not use actual game-starter QB, realized score state, or null play-caller fields as preseason features. All 544 historical forecasts explicitly record missing QB/play-caller reasons and Tier B confidence 0.80. Tier A is supported only with timestamped eligible context but remains historically unvalidated; Tier C uses league-dominant shrinkage and a 1.70 uncertainty scale.

blockedBy: No exact stored play-by-play or weekly-stat snapshots for the required historical folds have available_at timestamps at or before their simulated preseason cutoffs. The 2025 fold rejects late snapshot IDs 2524, 2526, 2527, 2530, 2531, 2534, 2535, 2538, 2539, 2540, 2542, 2543, and 2544. An immutable eligible archive or a user-approved specification change is required before fitting can be accepted.

targets.name: Calibrate and verify team ceilings
acceptance: Rolling-origin results compare V2 with rolling-average and league-average baselines for every required pool.
P10/P50/P90 coverage and proper scoring results are reported overall and by context-change and fallback cohorts.
Fixed inputs and seed reproduce identical team forecasts.
No team opportunity result changes the live displayed projection during shadow mode.

waves.name: Player role allocation
waves.gateToAdvance: Every relevant teammate receives scenario-based, role-compatible shares that reconcile to the team pools, including changed-team, rookie, injury, and competition cases.

targets.name: Build effective-dated transaction and role-scenario contracts
acceptance: Transactions preserve player, from-team, to-team, effective date, type, source, and investment evidence where available.
Role scenarios separately represent active, starter, snap, route, target, rush, receiving, red-zone, end-zone, and goal-line shares.
Scenario probabilities are bounded, normalized, versioned, attributable, and as-of safe.
Manual overrides require author, timestamp, reason, affected component, previous value, and expiry.

targets.name: Learn and reconcile player allocations
acceptance: Historical transition priors cover departures, arrivals, rookies, injuries, committees, and role changes.
Allocations use role compatibility and every relevant teammate rather than equal redistribution or independent multipliers.
Player target, RB-target, carry, receiving-TD-opportunity, and rushing-TD-opportunity shares reconcile to documented team tolerances.
Unresolved competitions remain explicit scenarios and widen player uncertainty.

targets.name: Verify the Mike Evans Tampa Bay to San Francisco fixture
acceptance: Tampa Bay departure analysis uses route, target, end-zone, red-zone, expected-TD, and controlled with/without-player evidence.
San Francisco arrival inserts Evans into a pre-forecast team pool and jointly recalculates all affected teammate shares.
No actual Evans touchdown is copied from Tampa Bay to San Francisco and both teams reconcile independently.
Featured, standard, and limited-role scenarios are reproducible and explanations identify all meaningful upgrades and downgrades.

waves.name: Efficiency and touchdown share
waves.gateToAdvance: Volume, efficiency, touchdown opportunity, touchdown conversion, and availability are separately estimated and chronologically calibrated.

targets.name: Estimate contextual player efficiency
acceptance: Yards and receptions are estimated from eligible player, role, quarterback, team, and opponent evidence with sample-aware shrinkage.
Changed-team and rookie players do not inherit destination efficiency without an explicit scenario and prior.
No automatic workload penalty is applied; volume, efficiency, and availability remain separate components.
Derivations expose source coverage, samples, priors, adjustments, and confidence.

targets.name: Separate touchdown opportunity from conversion
acceptance: Receiving and rushing touchdown opportunity derives from reconciled team pools and role-specific end-zone, red-zone, and goal-line evidence.
Conversion is regressed toward position, role, age, and sample priors while retaining validated persistent skill.
Raw prior-year touchdowns are not redistributed or carried forward directly.
Expected touchdowns reconcile to team passing and rushing touchdown pools within documented tolerances.

targets.name: Calibrate efficiency and touchdown cohorts
acceptance: Chronological results report yardage, reception, and touchdown calibration overall and by position, role, rookie, changed-team, injury, and sample-size cohort.
Touchdown-opportunity and conversion ablations are compared separately.
Mike Evans fixture outputs remain within the same general model contract with no player-specific branch.
Failed or inconclusive cohorts remain shadow and are not hidden by aggregate results.

waves.name: Weekly outcomes and roster simulation
waves.gateToAdvance: Every draftable player has calibrated weekly stat and fantasy distributions, and redraft and Best Ball consume those identical football inputs correctly.

targets.name: Generate weekly player and availability distributions
acceptance: Every draftable player has Weeks 1-17 active probability and P10, P25, median, mean, P75, and P90 fantasy distributions.
Availability is modeled separately from points conditional on being active.
Weekly stat lines reproduce scoring totals and position-aware spike and yardage-bonus probabilities.
Distribution monotonicity, finite outputs, fallback behavior, and deterministic seeds pass automated tests.

targets.name: Integrate shared distributions with redraft
acceptance: Redraft season projections aggregate the shared weekly distributions under each selected scoring contract.
Active-game rate, availability, season P10/P50/P90, changed-team scenario spread, confidence, and derivation are persisted.
Shadow results do not alter the live redraft order before promotion.
The redraft UI and downstream advisors read the persisted shared projection artifact rather than recomputing it differently.

targets.name: Integrate shared distributions with Best Ball
acceptance: Weekly stat draws use exact current DraftKings scoring and select the maximum legal 1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE, and 1 FLEX lineup.
Outputs include counted points, counted weeks, bye coverage, spike capture, roster P90, correlation effect, and candidate marginal value.
Save/resume and fixed-seed replay reproduce the same draft decision snapshot.
Existing partial shadow simulation is independently verified against roster-aware weekly inputs rather than accepted from code existence alone.

targets.name: Estimate and apply weekly correlation
acceptance: Same-team and opponent correlations use residual weekly outcomes, relationship priors, minimum samples, and hierarchical shrinkage.
The simulation uses a valid positive-semidefinite correlation structure.
Weak or missing pair evidence falls back visibly to a relationship prior with reduced confidence.
Correlation value is measured through counted roster outcomes rather than an unexplained boost.

waves.name: Validation and promotion decision
waves.gateToAdvance: The preregistered evidence supports an explicit PROMOTE decision; otherwise V2 is revised or retained in shadow mode.

targets.name: Run champion, market, challenger, and ablation comparisons
acceptance: All preregistered metrics, cohort slices, sample sizes, and paired confidence intervals are reported from chronological holdouts.
Overall season-total bias is within the approved tolerance and material cohort failures are visible.
V2 improves or meaningfully complements at least one primary roster or decision metric without materially degrading the others.
Real 2026 shadow decisions are collected without tuning on their outcomes.

targets.name: Record the promotion verdict
acceptance: The decision is explicitly PROMOTE, REVISE, or RETAIN with linked evidence and known limitations.
Any inconclusive comparison, leakage failure, reconciliation failure, or required cohort failure prevents promotion.
The chosen champion model and rollback artifact are versioned and reproducible.
Promotion requires explicit user authorization after reviewing the evidence.

waves.name: Product delivery and activation
